name: open-my-app
description: OpenMyApp — a Spotlight-style minimalist app launcher for macOS (pinyin search for apps and System Settings)

changes: Folder command results now rank shallower directories first within each match tier (e.g. ~/work before ~/work/xxx/work)

Built-in commands act as fallbacks: binding terminal or open to another app in Settings → Folder Commands now redirects their aliases (t / o) to that app as well; the built-in Terminal / Finder behavior remains when nothing is bound
Command results (t / o / custom prefixes) render as a list again instead of inheriting the empty-query app grid
Folder Commands settings: rows now show Command instead of Prefix, and long command names (e.g. terminal) keep a single-line row
Launchpad-style app grid: opening the panel with an empty query shows all installed apps as a 7-column icon grid sorted by most used; ←/→/↑/↓ move the selection, Return launches it
Custom folder commands: bind any prefix to any installed app in Settings → Folder Commands (e.g. zcode → iTerm); a unique abbreviation of the prefix works too (z → zcode)
Directory command ranking is now staged through Spotlight: exact name matches first, then prefix matches, then substring matches; / anchors match names starting or ending with the keyword
Clipboard cleanup is configurable in Settings → Clipboard (retention days and usage threshold) and new parameters apply immediately
Settings window reorganized into tabs: General / Hotkeys / Folder Commands / Clipboard / About
Unit test suite now runs on every push (pre-push hook) and in the release CI before building
Launch at login is now enabled by default on first launch; it can still be turned off anytime in Settings → General
Normal mode no longer shows recent clipboard items when the panel opens with an empty query; summoning the panel starts clean again, clipboard browsing stays in clipboard mode (⌘⇧V)
Clipboard history: every copy (text, images, files) is captured into a local SQLite database; large texts and images are stored as files with references, duplicates merge into one entry
Clipboard hits appear in search results (up to 3 per source) with instant in-memory matching plus async full-text search (FTS5, whitespace-split tokens, case-insensitive)
Pressing Return on a clipboard item copies it back and auto-pastes into the frontmost app (asks for Accessibility permission; copy-only until granted)
New clipboard-only mode on ⌘⇧V (customizable) showing recent records; low-usage records older than a week are cleaned up automatically
Large images get fast downsampled thumbnails for the results list
The search box is cleared every time the panel opens, and ⌘A now selects all text
The full words also trigger the commands: `terminal <name>` (same as `t <name>`) and `open <name>` (same as `o <name>`)
Command results elide the shared path prefix with `.../` so the distinguishing tail of each path is always visible (full path in tooltip)
File commands now exclude common dependency and build directories (node_modules, target, DerivedData, Pods, etc.) so results surface real project files
New `t <name>` and `o <name>` commands: open a matching folder in Terminal, or a file/folder in Finder
Spotlight-backed file search under the home directory, debounced input, capped at 5 results, paths shortened with ~
Bilingual UI: English and Simplified Chinese, following the system language
In-app updates: check for new versions in Settings, with automatic download, install, and relaunch
Update check falls back to a redirect-based probe when the GitHub API is rate-limited
Fix the result list height formula so the panel fits rows exactly (a 10pt shortfall caused a scrollbar)
Fix the leftover titlebar gap at the top of the panel; the search field is now vertically centered (panel switched to borderless style)
Initial release: Spotlight-style floating search box, shown on launch
Search local apps by full pinyin, pinyin initials, or English name
Search and open System Settings panes directly
Global ⌥Space hotkey; auto-hide on outside click
Menu bar resident with hideable icon to save menu bar space
